board/goal-status tests: after a committed close the goals list card reads Done and the board header stage reads Closed (STAGE_WORDS) - asserted through the real decoders on a frame the daemon emits (recorded from the live drive, not hand-written).

Playwright journey against a REAL daemon (tests/e2e/control-room/): a contract-bearing goal driven to readiness (acceptance fixtures through the real command path) -> Needs you -> Close -> Done; `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted.

Live drive on UnAI: one goal closed from the browser (GoalCompleted event id, the coverage read n/n VERIFIED, the affordance read showing the goal.close offer before and its absence after) in a row comment; if no UnAI goal is ready, the exact GOAL_CLOSE_* refusal and the unverified criterion ids are recorded instead - never a fabricated close.

README 'Review loop' / 'What runs today' clause and docs/agent-stack-runbook.md name what closes a goal on the live loop and the GOAL_CLOSE_* refusal family; gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: NO DAEMON PRODUCTION CHANGE: if a daemon edit is needed, the gap belongs to child 1 or 2 - stop, comment on that child, report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds.

implementationPlan.description: THE READY CARD AND ITS TWO STATES, in apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/needs-you-model.ts (:110-135 derives READY_TO_CLOSE from coverage totals — criteria > 0 && verified === criteria && nothing pending — and attaches `close: { affordance }` ONLY when /affordances/read offers goal.close). Assert BOTH states, because the difference between them is the whole point: (a) coverage n/n VERIFIED **and** the surface offers goal.close -> the card renders WITH the Close action; (b) the same coverage but NO offer -> the card renders with the existing 'The daemon is not offering to close it yet; open the goal to see why' detail and NO action. State (b) is the one that matters: a dead button that dispatches into a refusal is worse than an honest explanation, and the model already draws that distinction — this row must not erase it. Update the fixtures to the daemon's REAL offer shape (task rail 3); the exact-key decoders reject anything hand-written, so a synthetic fixture fails at the decoder and reads as a test bug.

The `approval.decide` path DOES write a scope, so the contract-LESS journey closes end to end today (arm :451, full authenticated wire, GoalCompleted x1).
